meta.purpose: Questions that must be answered before a decision is reasonable, each with the information needed and the state of the answer. Q-15 to Q-22 were added by the integration pass after a second verification run.
meta.rule: A blocked question is not a reason to guess. It is a reason to leave the value blank and say so.

questions.question: Do the five supplied short links actually carry the tracking ID shopnow047c-20?
questions.needed_info: The Associates click report, or a resolved URL visibly containing the tag parameter, for each link.
questions.answer: Unknown.
questions.how_to_unblock: Open each link while signed in to the Associates dashboard and check that the click registers under shopnow047c-20.

questions.question: Are link.amazon short links compliant Special Links?
questions.needed_info: An official statement from Amazon on this specific redirector, or a tracked click observed end to end.
questions.answer: Unresolved. No official source either permits or prohibits this specific host in a way this session can cite, and no tracked click could be observed.
questions.how_to_unblock: Test one link through the Associates workflow. If the click appears in the report, it is functioning as a Special Link. That is a measurement, not a ruling.

questions.question: What is the valid ASIN for each of the five products?
questions.needed_info: The ten-character ASIN shown on each product page and in the owner's Associates record.
questions.answer: All five redirect targets were observed on 2026-11-20; the intended ASINs remain unconfirmed.
questions.how_to_unblock: Confirm the intended ASIN and listing with the Associates account records for each product.

questions.question: What commission rate applies to each product?
questions.needed_info: The Standard Commission Income schedule for Home & Kitchen and for the thermometer category.
questions.answer: Not recorded. The rate card URL redirects to an Associates sign-in page.
questions.how_to_unblock: Read the rate card while signed in. Do not publish a rate until then.

questions.question: What do these appliances cost, and are they in stock?
questions.needed_info: Price and availability served by Amazon through a link it serves, or through the Creators API / PA API.
questions.answer: Not published, because publishing it without that feed is prohibited, not merely unverified.
questions.how_to_unblock: Connect the Creators API or PA API, or embed an Amazon-served widget that carries the price.

questions.question: Which of these appliances is best?
questions.needed_info: Independent measurement, or a stated, disclosed testing method performed by this site.
questions.answer: No winner is declared. This site has not tested any product and says so on every guide.
questions.how_to_unblock: Either purchase and test units and publish the method, or keep the site in its current advisory mode. Do not synthesise a verdict from listing titles.

questions.question: Would any of these products appeal to readers enough to click?
questions.needed_info: Outbound click data from a first-party endpoint, over a meaningful window.
questions.answer: No data exists yet. The ledger is intentionally empty.
questions.how_to_unblock: Choose a first-party host, deploy the documented collector, then wait for enough sessions to mean anything.

questions.question: Which guide topic should be written next?
questions.needed_info: Search Console query impressions, and the click-through rate of existing guides.
questions.answer: Undetermined. Four guides are published as hypotheses; none has been measured.
questions.how_to_unblock: Verify the site in Search Console, submit the sitemap, and revisit after four to six weeks.

questions.question: Under what name should the site publish, and who is the author?
questions.needed_info: A real legal or pen name, a short bio, and a decision on whether to disclose testing or not.
questions.answer: Undetermined. No author identity is published, because inventing one would be a fabrication.
questions.how_to_unblock: Supply the name and a two-sentence bio. Then an author page and a real byline can be published.

questions.question: Is the site allowed to show Amazon product photographs?
questions.needed_info: Either an Amazon-served widget that carries the image, or API image fields used unmodified under the IP License.
questions.answer: Not established for this site. Program Content may not be altered, and this site has no licensed feed.
questions.how_to_unblock: Enrol the API, or use Amazon-served link formats, and then place images unmodified.

questions.question: Does the FTC require the disclosure to be a specific wording?
questions.needed_info: The FTC's own guidance on affiliate disclosure wording and placement.
questions.answer: Answered. The FTC gives example wording and says the disclosure must be clear and conspicuous, and that the reader must be able to weigh the recommendation. Nearby 'paid link' labelling is described as adequate.
questions.how_to_unblock: n/a

questions.question: May this site display price comparison tables?
questions.needed_info: The Associates Program rules on price display, including the comparison-format clause.
questions.answer: Answered as a constraint. A price may be shown only if Amazon serves it or it arrives via the API, and a comparison format must show both the lowest new and, if provided, lowest used price. This site shows neither.
questions.how_to_unblock: n/a

questions.question: What was in this repository before this session?
questions.needed_info: Git history and working tree.
questions.answer: Answered. One commit, one eight-byte README. No site, no prior pages, no data. The 'existing site' referenced in the brief is not in this repository.
questions.how_to_unblock: n/a

questions.question: Will the five links stay pointed at the same products?
questions.needed_info: A dated re-check of each redirect, repeated over time.
questions.answer: Unknown over time. Each row is a single observation on one date.
questions.how_to_unblock: Re-run tools/validate.py monthly and diff the observed targets against products.json.

questions.question: Do the five submitted links resolve to Amazon product pages at all?
questions.needed_info: Two independent fetch passes, recorded with the date and the destination each request returned.
questions.answer: Answered by this pass. Four of five reach a product page: B0CDY277D3 (CHEFMAN dual basket), B09B7SB46R (Emeril Lagasse French door), B08DKYBTPH (Chefman 8 Qt) and B0DZFD6R9Z (CHEF iQ Sense thermometer). One — B0c8moW59 — has never reached anything but Amazon's continue-shopping interstitial. Earlier registers in this repository disagreed about exactly these rows, which is why the second pass was run.
questions.how_to_unblock: Nothing to unblock. Re-run the fetch on a schedule (SUG-24) and let the register update; treat every destination as an observation with a date, not a permanent fact.

questions.question: What are the five products, by name and category?
questions.needed_info: The listing title and breadcrumb from each destination page.
questions.answer: Recorded for the four that resolved, transcribed from the destination page itself. Four are air fryers in Home & Kitchen › Kitchen & Dining › Small Appliances › Fryers › Air Fryers; one is a meat thermometer under Thermometers & Timers › Meat. The fifth row has no name, because no listing was reached.
questions.how_to_unblock: Nothing. If the owner meant a different product by the 9-character code, that correction changes the register and every page built from it.

questions.question: Is the GitHub Pages deployment currently healthy?
questions.needed_info: The Actions run history and the Pages build type, not a guess from the URL loading.
questions.answer: It was not. Every push to main ran the deploy workflow's validation step and failed, so the Actions deployment was skipped and the site was being served only by the repository's legacy branch build — a red check on a live URL, which looks fine and proves nothing. This pass replaced the ad-hoc check with the real validator and added a mount-path check.
questions.how_to_unblock: Confirm the next deploy goes green, and decide whether Pages should be served by Actions (build-then-publish) or by the branch build. Both are live in this repository at once today, which is the actual defect.

questions.question: How many versions of this site exist, and which one publishes?
questions.needed_info: A count of competing front pages, stylesheets and navigation shells.
questions.answer: Five had accumulated at the root of main: a Good Measure Kitchen storefront, a /crisp/ publication, two further CSS/JS shells and an archive of older attempts. The integration pass promoted one publication to the root, moved the rest to archive/ untouched, and made the archive non-indexable. One brand, one nav, one stylesheet, one disclosure template.
questions.how_to_unblock: Nothing for the owner. Future sessions should extend the published surface via src/data and tools/build.py rather than adding a second front page alongside it.

questions.question: Is there any traffic data at all to choose the next topic from?
questions.needed_info: Search Console query data for the published property, or an equivalent first-party source.
questions.answer: Unknown. No property is verified in this repository, no analytics endpoint is deployed, and the campaign ledger is empty by design. The topic queue on /topics/ is therefore stated as reasoning, not as demand.
questions.how_to_unblock: Verify the property, wait for four weeks of queries, then re-order the queue. Any 'high search volume' claim made before that would be invented.

questions.question: What is the production hostname, and does the canonical URL match it?
questions.needed_info: A decision: publish at karagemop466-tech.github.io/Affil1/ or point a custom domain at the repository.
questions.answer: Unknown, and it matters. Every canonical tag, sitemap entry and feed link is currently written for the github.io project path. A custom domain without rebuilding the data layer would leave the site canonicalising to a host it no longer lives on.
questions.how_to_unblock: Decide the host. SITE_ROOT in tools/build.py is the single place to change; the build rewrites every page, sitemap and feed from it, and tools/validate.py fails the build if a canonical drifts outside that base.

questions.question: Who signs off a guide before it publishes, and against what?
questions.needed_info: A named reviewer, or an accepted decision that the CI gate is the reviewer.
questions.answer: No human reviewer exists. Today the automated gate checks structure — disclosure present, links sponsored and marked, no price figures, images resolve, sitemap agreement — and cannot check whether a sentence is true. The signature line in PUBLISHING_WORKFLOW.md is still blank in the built pages, and the compliance table says so.
questions.how_to_unblock: Either name a reviewer or record, publicly, that publication is gated by the automated checks and the flagged register alone.

questions.question: What does the owner want the site to optimise for in the next 60 days?
questions.needed_info: A stated priority: traffic, list building, revenue per visit, or a compliance clean-up before scaling.
questions.answer: Unknown from anything in the repository, and the difference changes the order of the board. A traffic priority means publishing volume plus Search Console; a revenue priority means the Special Link test and the one-link experiment first; a trust priority means an author, a corrections log and real photography.
questions.how_to_unblock: Pick one of the three in /suggestions/. The board is sorted so that the first two rows are worth more than the next ten combined.
